content.user_title: Run and Fix Project Lint Errors
content.value_statement: Lint issues can slow development and leave code quality problems unresolved. This skill runs the project lint workflow, applies small fixes, and checks the result again.
actual_capabilities: Runs the repository lint command documented by the project.
Uses autofix when the repository provides an autofix option.
Captures lint errors that remain after automated fixes.
Applies small, idiomatic fixes to remaining lint issues.
Re-runs lint and reviews the resulting changes.
limitations: It depends on the repository documentation and configured lint scripts.
It does not guarantee that every lint issue can be fixed automatically.
It does not commit or stage changes.
It does not replace tests, code review, or a merge gate.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Run the project linter, apply focused fixes, and verify the branch before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Reviewable Diff
use_cases.description: Resolve routine lint errors with minimal changes so reviewers can focus on behavior and design.

use_cases.title: Standardize Maintenance Work
use_cases.description: Repeat the documented lint workflow after maintenance edits and record any issues that still need manual work.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Project Linter
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the repository's documented lint command. Report the command used, the errors found, and whether the run passes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Lint Autofixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the documented lint command with autofix when supported. Review the changes, then report any remaining lint errors.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Remaining Lint Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint with the repository's preferred autofix option, fix remaining issues with minimal idiomatic changes, and run lint again.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Clean Lint Diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete the repository lint workflow, inspect the final diff for unrelated changes, and summarize unresolved issues without staging or committing.

output_examples.input: Run the documented lint workflow and fix any remaining issues.
output: Lint completed successfully after the documented autofix step.
The final diff contains only focused formatting and rule-compliance changes.
No changes were staged or committed.

output_examples.input: Check the branch for lint errors before review.
output_examples.output: The lint command still reports two manual issues. The affected files and error messages are listed, and no unrelated configuration changes were made.

best_practices: Follow the lint command documented by the repository.
Keep fixes small and review the diff after autofix.
Run lint again after manual changes and report unresolved errors.
anti_patterns: Do not change lint configuration without evidence that the change is required.
Do not hide errors with broad suppressions or unrelated refactoring.
Do not stage, commit, or present a failed lint run as clean.

faq.question: Does this skill run lint automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It follows the lint command documented by the repository.

faq.question: Will it apply autofixes?
faq.answer: Yes, when the repository provides a documented autofix option.

faq.question: Does it fix every reported issue?
faq.answer: No. It fixes small, clear issues and reports problems that require further judgment.

faq.question: Does it change lint configuration?
faq.answer: Only when repository evidence shows that a configuration change belongs in the project.

faq.question: Does it stage or commit changes?
faq.answer: No. The workflow leaves staging and commits to the user.

faq.question: Is a clean lint run a complete code review?
faq.answer: No. Lint checks are useful, but they do not replace tests, review, or a merge gate.
